title: Super Mario Party Jamboree
description: Super Mario Party Jamboree is the third major Mario Party release for Nintendo Switch and the largest of the three. It features seven boards, more than 110 minigames, 22 playable characters, Jamboree Buddies, Pro Rules, a solo Party-Planner Trek and several specialized local/online modes.

nintendoNotes:
Nintendo lists the original Nintendo Switch download at 5.4 GB, with support for TV, Tabletop and Handheld modes. Single-system player count is 1-4 and online player count can reach 20 depending on mode. Nintendo Switch Online and a Nintendo Account are required for online features. Save Data Cloud is supported.

Motion-control minigames require compatible Joy-Con controllers. Nintendo Switch Lite can run the software, but motion-control features may require separate compatible controllers and some motion-focused modes have limitations. The physical Nintendo Switch release is a normal game card and does not require a mandatory full-game download.

The Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Jamboree TV Upgrade Pack is a separate $19.99 USD purchase for Nintendo Switch 2. It is not required for the original Switch game.

gameplayPillars.title: Mario Party Board Competition
gameplayPillars.description: The main Mario Party mode uses the familiar turn-based board structure: roll, move, gather coins, buy Stars, use items and react to board-specific events. Each of the seven boards has a distinct economy and route structure. Rainbow Galleria revolves around a multi-level shopping mall, Goomba Lagoon changes routes with tides, Roll 'em Raceway emphasizes speed and movement items, Mega Wiggler's Tree Party revolves around shifting paths around Wiggler, and King Bowser's Keep introduces more aggressive Bowser hazards. Western Land and Mario's Rainbow Castle return from earlier games with modern systems.

gameplayPillars.title: Jamboree Buddies and Pro Rules
gameplayPillars.description: Ten characters can become Jamboree Buddies after a player wins their showdown minigame: Mario, Luigi, Peach, Daisy, Wario, Waluigi, Yoshi, Rosalina, Donkey Kong and Bowser Jr. Buddies temporarily travel with the winning player and apply character-specific advantages. Pro Rules provide a more competitive alternative to standard rules by reducing selected random elements and revealing information such as the bonus-star category.

gameplayPillars.title: Large-Scale and Side Modes
gameplayPillars.description: Koopathlon is a 20-player online race where minigame scores convert to movement. Bowser Kaboom Squad is an eight-player online cooperative battle against Impostor Bowser. Minigame Bay organizes direct minigame competition. Rhythm Kitchen uses motion controls in cooperative rhythm cooking, Toad's Item Factory focuses on motion-driven puzzles, and Paratroopa Flight School uses two Joy-Con controllers for wing-like motion input. Party-Planner Trek gives solo players a structured progression mode.

worldSummary: The game is organized around Party Plaza and a resort-like archipelago of activity islands. A hot-air balloon gives access to Mario Party boards and side modes. The seven main boards range from a tropical tidal lagoon and giant shopping mall to a racetrack, giant Wiggler forest and dangerous Bowser fortress. Two boards revisit classic locations: Western Land from Mario Party 2 and Mario's Rainbow Castle from the original Mario Party.

storyChapters.title: Party Plaza and Party-Planner Trek
storyChapters.body: Party-Planner Trek is the game's primary structured solo progression experience. The player explores board areas between tasks, speaks with Mushroom Kingdom characters, completes requests and enters minigames. Objectives award Mini Stars and decorative rewards for Party Plaza. It functions as a guided tour through Jamboree's boards and mechanics rather than a conventional narrative campaign.

storyChapters.title: Seven Mario Party Boards
storyChapters.body: Mario Party mode is built around seven boards. Five are new: Mega Wiggler's Tree Party, Roll 'em Raceway, Goomba Lagoon, Rainbow Galleria and King Bowser's Keep. Western Land returns from Mario Party 2, while Mario's Rainbow Castle returns from the original Mario Party. Each board changes movement, items and route decisions through distinct events and economies.

storyChapters.title: Bowser Challenges and Minigame Islands
storyChapters.body: Bowser Kaboom Squad and Koopathlon are the headline large-scale online modes. Bowser Kaboom Squad asks eight players to cooperate, collect bombs and load cannons while surviving Impostor Bowser. Koopathlon supports up to twenty racers; performance in rapid solo minigames advances each player, with periodic Bowser survival events capable of changing positions dramatically.

perfNotes:
Independent technical comparisons consistently describe the original Nintendo Switch version at approximately 1080p in TV mode and 720p in handheld mode, targeting 60 FPS. Nintendo Life specifically praised a slick frame rate across docked and handheld play. The game does not support HDR or VRR on original Switch.

These values describe the Switch 1 release and must not be confused with Jamboree TV or the optional Switch 2 Edition, which has separate presentation behavior.

handheld.notes: Nintendo Switch 2 Edition, Version 2.2.0 or later. Nintendo officially lists Full HD (1080p) handheld/tabletop output for Jamboree TV. The base Super Mario Party Jamboree selection in the Switch 2 Edition also received 1080p video output in Version 2.2.0. Technical reviews consistently report a 60 FPS presentation.

tv.mode: Base Super Mario Party Jamboree – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition
tv.notes: For the base Super Mario Party Jamboree selection inside the Nintendo Switch 2 Edition, Version 2.2.0 or later outputs 1080p (FHD). Jamboree TV is a separate Switch 2-exclusive mode and supports WQHD 2560x1440 in TV mode. Technical reviews report 60 FPS for both the 1080p base presentation and 1440p Jamboree TV.

modes.name: Base Super Mario Party Jamboree – Switch 2 Edition
modes.notes: Base Super Mario Party Jamboree selected from the Nintendo Switch 2 Edition title screen. Nintendo's Version 2.2.0 patch notes explicitly state that video output is 1080p (FHD). The Switch 2 Edition is required for this higher-resolution mode.

modes.name: Jamboree TV
modes.notes: Jamboree TV is exclusive to the Nintendo Switch 2 Edition. Nintendo officially specifies WQHD (1440p) TV output and Full HD (1080p) handheld/tabletop output. Independent technical reviews consistently report 60 FPS.

faq.q: How many boards and minigames are in Super Mario Party Jamboree?
faq.a: There are seven Mario Party boards and more than 110 minigames. Five boards are new to Jamboree, while Western Land and Mario's Rainbow Castle return from earlier Mario Party games.

Player count depends on mode. Mario Party and Minigame Bay support up to four players. Bowser Kaboom Squad can support up to eight online players. Koopathlon can support up to twenty online players. Some side modes are local-only or have controller/system restrictions.

faq.q: Does the Nintendo Switch version require Nintendo Switch Online?
faq.a: Nintendo Switch Online is not required for normal offline/local gameplay. It is required for internet multiplayer. Save Data Cloud is also supported through Nintendo Switch Online.

verdictSummary: Super Mario Party Jamboree is the most complete Mario Party package created for the original Nintendo Switch. Its strongest achievement is the combination of seven strong boards, more than 110 minigames, Jamboree Buddies, Pro Rules and flexible control settings. Large-scale online modes are valuable additions rather than replacements for the core board game, while Party-Planner Trek makes solo play more viable than in many previous entries.
verdictPros: Excellent seven-board selection with five new boards and two returning classics
More than 110 minigames and unusually broad local/online mode variety
Jamboree Buddies and Pro Rules add meaningful strategy to the modern Mario Party formula
verdictCons: Full board matches can be long
Player counts and controller requirements vary significantly by mode
The biggest online modes require one player per system and Nintendo Switch Online

reviews.quote: Metacritic aggregates the Nintendo Switch release at 82/100, indicating generally favorable critical reception.
OpenCritic aggregates the game at approximately 81/100 with a strong majority of critics recommending it.
Nintendo Life awarded 9/10, praising the minigame selection, boards, visual presentation, performance and improvements to the core Mario Party formula.

timeline.title: Announcement
timeline.body: Nintendo revealed Super Mario Party Jamboree during the June 18, 2024 Nintendo Direct, announcing seven boards, more than 110 minigames and 20-player Koopathlon.

timeline.title: Nintendo Switch Worldwide Release
timeline.body: The original Nintendo Switch version launched worldwide on October 17, 2024.

timeline.title: Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Jamboree TV Upgrade
timeline.body: Nintendo released Super Mario Party Jamboree – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Jamboree TV and its paid Upgrade Pack on July 24, 2025. The original Switch game remains a separate fully playable product.

patchNotes.body: Version 2.3.0 fixed Nintendo Switch issues including scoring behavior in Three Throw and an item bug involving Mushroom Tickets, while also adding Switch 2-side language support and general improvements.
Version 2.2.0 introduced Switch 2-specific presentation adjustments for upgraded software and additional general fixes. Original Nintendo Switch received general gameplay-experience fixes.
Version 1.1.1 fixed an online Minigame Bay Tag Match issue that could terminate sessions depending on the room creator's nickname length.

studioAbout: Nintendo Cube—formerly known as NDcube—is the Nintendo-affiliated studio responsible for modern Mario Party development. Super Mario Party Jamboree was developed by Nintendo Cube and published by Nintendo, continuing the studio's focus on board-game and multiplayer-oriented Nintendo software.
